plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid above my value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value (negative profit). If I bid below, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. With a value of $46, I should bid exactly $46 to ensure optimal outcomes.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this setup, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $17, I should bid exactly $17 to maximize expected profit, regardless of what others bid.

This is a second-price auction format (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, as this ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no history to adjust from, I'll bid my true value of $28.
